Subject: POC kickoff — scheduling and sample payloads

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're ready to lock in a POC kickoff with hands-on work: prompt review, routing scenarios, and a couple of load passes. Our engineering and data teams will join.

A couple of asks up front so we can prep:
- Can you share a short sample payload template and a redaction checklist we should apply to our data before upload?
- We want to exercise routing (tiered model fallbacks) and a realistic load pattern (burst + steady). Is there a recommended load-plan format you accept?
- Proposed weeks: Aug 10–14 or Aug 17–21. Which days/times work for Redwood? We prefer mornings PT.

I'll also note two people who will be on the thread: Natalie Cho (product) and I can circulate internal samples once we get the checklist.

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: Re: POC kickoff — scheduling and sample payloads

Hi Alex — great to hear. Morning PT works for us. Proposed slots (PT):
- Tue Aug 11, 09:30–11:30 — kickoff + prompt review (30–45m) then hands-on routing plays
- Thu Aug 13, 09:00–11:00 — load tests and evaluation runs

Please confirm which pair you'd prefer (we'll hold both until you pick).

Attached are the artifacts to help you prepare:
- redaction_checklist.pdf (short checklist: PII, tokens, encryption hints)
- sample_payload_template.csv (columns: id, prompt, metadata.json, expected_label)
- load_plan.md (example steady + burst patterns we usually run)
- MAP-v1.docx (mutual action plan template — blank)

Notes on expectations and asks from your side:
- Redact PII and replace with deterministic markers (we list examples in the checklist).
- Provide 200–500 sample prompts for the hands-on prompt review; mark a 30–50 item evaluation set for quality checks.
- For routing tests: include a field in metadata.json called "routing_hint" with values like "low_cost", "high_accuracy". We'll map those to model variants during the session.

Karthik and Marissa — can you take the lead on routing/playbook and load-test orchestration? Karthik, please confirm the throughput targets you can simulate and any token limits we should warn the customer about. Marissa, would you own the prompt evaluation checklist and analytics dashboard for the session?

Alex — I'll also share a Drive folder link once you confirm a slot so you can drop the redacted CSV there.

Thanks,
Tessa

--

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: DataHalo POC — prep checklist and who does what

Karthik / Marissa — following my reply to DataHalo, here are the concrete asks so we can move quickly once they pick a slot. Please reply with availability and confirmations.

1) Routing/playbook (Karthik)
- Prepare two model variants for the session: "high_accuracy" (larger model) and "low_cost" (quantized smaller model).
- We'll wire up routing via the "routing_hint" metadata field Alex will include.
- Load targets: simulate a steady 10 qps for 10 minutes and two 60-second bursts at 40 qps. Can you confirm we can run that in the Dedicated sandbox?
- Bring an outline of fallback behavior and metrics we'll expose (latency P50/P95, token cost estimate, error rate).

2) Prompt evaluation & dashboards (Marissa)
- Prepare the evaluation template (CSV) and a short rubric for pass/fail on hallucination, accuracy, and formatting.
- Set up a dashboard view in the console for the session showing per-prompt quality and token breakdown.

3) Logistics
- I'll create a Drive folder and invite Alex/Natalie and request their redacted sample CSV.
- Bring MAP-v1 draft as a starting point for scoping deliverables and success criteria.

Small items: ensure we have a Zoom link and record the session; prepare an ops runbook for rolling back routing changes if needed.

Can you both reply by EOD with: (a) confirmation on load targets, (b) who will own the dashboard widgets, (c) any blockers?

Thanks — Tessa
